Total_Fitness

Brandie QC

2026-02-12

Code for Analyzing Total Fitness

Equation: p(Establishment)p(Surv to Rep - y1)Fruits(y1) + p(Winter Surv)p(Surv to Rep - y2)Fruits(y2)

Calculated at the individual level

phi_function <- function(model) {
    phi <- sum(residuals(model, type="pearson")^2)/df.residual(model) 
    return(phi)
} #function for calculating the overdispersion paramter (for quasi-poisson)

sem <- function(x, na.rm=FALSE) {           #for calculating standard error
  sd(x,na.rm=na.rm)/sqrt(length(na.omit(x)))
}

Calculate Total Fitness

wl2_total_fitness <- left_join(wl2_establishment, wl2_surv_to_rep_y1) %>% 
  left_join(wl2_fruits_y1) %>% 
  select(-death.date, -bud.date) %>% #remove y1 death and bud dates 
  mutate(mf=as.numeric(mf), rep=as.numeric(rep)) %>% #convert these cols to numeric for merging 
  left_join(winter_surv) %>% 
  select(-death.date) %>% 
  left_join(wl2_surv_to_rep_y2) %>% 
  left_join(wl2_fruits_y2) %>% 
  select(-death.date) %>% 
  mutate(SurvtoRep_Y1=if_else(is.na(SurvtoRep_Y1), 0, SurvtoRep_Y1),
         y1_fruits=if_else(is.na(y1_fruits), 0, y1_fruits),
         y2_fruits=if_else(is.na(y2_fruits), 0, y2_fruits),
         WinterSurv=if_else(is.na(WinterSurv), 0, WinterSurv),
         SurvtoRep_y2=if_else(is.na(SurvtoRep_y2), 0, SurvtoRep_y2)) %>% 
  mutate(Total_Fitness=(Establishment*SurvtoRep_Y1*y1_fruits) + (WinterSurv*SurvtoRep_y2*y2_fruits)) %>% 
  left_join(wl2_pretrans_size_all)

Try models with poisson and quasi-poisson

Basic model - Poisson and Quasi-Poisson

total_fecund_poisson <- glmer(Total_Fitness ~ height.cm + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block), 
                              family = poisson,
                              data=wl2_total_fitness_scaled)
## Warning in checkConv(attr(opt, "derivs"), opt$par, ctrl = control$checkConv, :
## Model failed to converge with max|grad| = 0.17707 (tol = 0.002, component 1)
## Warning in checkConv(attr(opt, "derivs"), opt$par, ctrl = control$checkConv, : Model is nearly unidentifiable: very large eigenvalue
##  - Rescale variables?
summary(total_fecund_poisson)
## Generalized linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood (Laplace
##   Approximation) [glmerMod]
##  Family: poisson  ( log )
## Formula: Total_Fitness ~ height.cm + (1 | pop/mf) + (1 | block)
##    Data: wl2_total_fitness_scaled
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   5060.5   5087.3  -2525.3   5050.5     1561 
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -5.8549 -0.4492 -0.0079 -0.0046 27.1310 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  mf:pop (Intercept)  3.52    1.876   
##  pop    (Intercept) 58.97    7.679   
##  block  (Intercept)  1.11    1.053   
## Number of obs: 1566, groups:  mf:pop, 148; pop, 23; block, 13
## 
## Fixed effects:
##               Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept) -1.021e+01  4.062e-04  -25126   <2e-16 ***
## height.cm    1.499e-01  4.062e-04     369   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##           (Intr)
## height.cm 0.000 
## optimizer (Nelder_Mead) convergence code: 0 (OK)
## Model failed to converge with max|grad| = 0.17707 (tol = 0.002, component 1)
## Model is nearly unidentifiable: very large eigenvalue
##  - Rescale variables?
plot(total_fecund_poisson, which = 1) #residuals plot 

#doesn't look great
deviance(total_fecund_poisson)/df.residual(total_fecund_poisson) #check for overdispersion (caused by excess of 0s)
## [1] 2.744567
##try quasi-poisson model to deal with the above (and based on the above plot)
##Can't directly use quasi families with glmer so have to use Ben Bolker's quasi-likelihood adjustment function:
#https://bbolker.github.io/mixedmodels-misc/glmmFAQ.html#fitting-models-with-overdispersion
#also got help from: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/68915173/how-do-i-fit-a-quasi-poisson-model-with-lme4-or-glmmtmb
quasi_table <- function(model,ctab=coef(summary(model))) {
    phi <- sum(residuals(model, type="pearson")^2)/df.residual(model) #overdispersion parameter
    qctab <- within(as.data.frame(ctab),
    {   `Std. Error` <- `Std. Error`*sqrt(phi)
        `z value` <- Estimate/`Std. Error`
        `Pr(>|z|)` <- 2*pnorm(abs(`z value`), lower.tail=FALSE)
    })
    return(qctab)
}
printCoefmat(quasi_table(total_fecund_poisson),digits=2)
##             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept) -1.0e+01    9.2e-04  -11051   <2e-16 ***
## height.cm    1.5e-01    9.2e-04     162   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#As specified, the estimates are identical; the standard errors and p-values have been appropriately inflated, the z-values have been appropriately deflated.

  "1_pop.block",      "Total_Fitness ~  height.cm_scaled + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block)", 
  "2_WY_Recent",      "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block)",
  "3_WY_Historical",  "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Historic_Wtr_Year_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Historic_Wtr_Year_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + (1|pop) + (1|block)",
  "4_GS_Recent",      "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Recent_GrwSsn_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Recent_GrwSsn_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block)", 
  "5_GS_Historical",  "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Historic_GrwSsn_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Historic_GrwSsn_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block)",
  "6_WY_Recent_height",      "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + height.cm_scaled + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block)",
  "7_WY_Historical_height",  "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Historic_Wtr_Year_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Historic_Wtr_Year_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + height.cm_scaled + (1|pop/mf) + (1|block)" ,
  "8_GS_Recent_height",      "Total_Fitness ~  AvgTempDist_Recent_GrwSsn_scaled + AvgPPTDist_Recent_GrwSsn_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + height.cm_scaled + (1|pop) + (1|block)",

)

#pairwise test between WL2 and BH (the pop with the highest total fitness):
wtr_yr_recent_mod <- glmer(Total_Fitness ~  AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled + Geographic_Dist_scaled + height.cm_scaled + (1|pop) + (1|block), 
                           family = poisson, data = wl2_total_fitness_scaled)
#get min and max GD
min(wl2_total_fitness_scaled$AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled) 
## [1] -1.353733
max(wl2_total_fitness_scaled$AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled)
## [1] 2.188742
minmaxGD = list(AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled = c(-1.358033, 2.153113))

# Calculate EMMs at the min and max GD
emm_results <- emmeans(wtr_yr_recent_mod, ~ AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled, at = minmaxGD)
# View the results
summary(emm_results)
##  AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled   emmean   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##                         -1.36 -10.0491 3.02 Inf    -15.98     -4.12
##                          2.15   0.0251 2.98 Inf     -5.82      5.87
## 
## Results are given on the log (not the response) scale. 
## Confidence level used: 0.95
# Perform pairwise comparison
pairs(emm_results) 
##  contrast                                                                      
##  (AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled-1.358033) - AvgGD_Recent_Wtr_Year_scaled2.153113
##  estimate   SE  df z.ratio p.value
##     -10.1 4.65 Inf  -2.167  0.0302
## 
## Results are given on the log (not the response) scale.
#P=0.0302
#but this is based off the poisson model, not the quasi-poisson...
